 JUDGMENT

This is petition filed under Section 164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of T. Prakash, who is son of petitioners No.1 and 2 and brother of petitioner No.3, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows :
On 03-08-2022 at about 2.30 p.m., the deceased T. Prakash was proceeding on Passion Pro motorcycle bearing No.AP-03-BJ-9190 towards Madanapalle.

At that time, when he was near coffee house, Punugupalli village, on Madanapalle-Tirupathi NH-71 road, Vayalpad Mandal, the driver of the Ford Ecosport car bearing No.AP-03-CB-3679 came from the opposite direction, in high speed, in rash and negligent manner.
Due to which, both the vehicles collided with each other and resulted in an accident.
Due to said impact, the deceased got fatal crushed injuries and died on the way to hospital.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was working as driver and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
He was contributing his entire earnings to his family.
Due to untimely death of a sole bread earner, the petitioners are struggling for their livelihood.
The Vayalpad Police have registered the case for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% per annum.

sentences.text: On service of notice to the respondents, the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
Whereas, the respondent No.2 did not choose to appear and remained absent.

Hence, the respondent No.2 is placed as ex-parte.
4.
The respondent No.1 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of Ford Eco Sport car bearing No.AP-03-CB-3679 and its validity as on the date of accident.
It seeks protection under Sections 147 and 149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It has contended that, the petition is bad for non compliance of provision under Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.

It has contended that, the Ford Eco Sport car bearing No.AP-03-CB- 3679 was not at all involved in the alleged accident and the alleged accident took place due to the negligence on the part of the deceased himself.

It has further contended that, the claim petition is liable to the dismissed for non-joinder of necessary parties, as the driver of Ford Eco Sport car bearing No.AP-03-CB-3679 was not made as party to the proceedings.

It has contended that, the driver of the offending car was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and the said car was not having valid permit and fitness certificate as on the date of accident.
It has denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and relationship of petitioners with the deceased.
Further, it has sought for permission to contest even on behalf of respondent No.2 under Section 170 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Further it is contended that, the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant.
For the above denials and contentions, it prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioners prove that, T. Prakash has succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident, alleged to have occurred on 03-08-2022 at about 2.30 p.m., on Madanapalle- Tirupathi NH-71 road, near coffee house, Punugupalli village, Vayalpad Mandal,
Annamaya District, Andra Pradesh, due to involvement of Ford Ecosport Car bearing Reg. No. AP-03- CB-3679 ?

2. Whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation? If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3. What order or Award ?
6.

On the other hand, the respondent No.1 has got examined its Deputy Manager as R.W.1 and no documents have been got marked by it.

sentences.text: I have heard the arguments of both the sides and perused the entire material placed on record.

8. My findings on the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 9. Issue No.1: It is the specific case of the petitioners that, on 03-08-2022 at about 2.30 p.m., the deceased T. Prakash was proceeding on Passion Pro motorcycle bearing No.AP-03-BJ-9190 towards Madanapalle.

At that time, when he was near coffee house, Punugupalli village, on Madanapalle-Tirupathi NH-71 road, Vayalpad Mandal, the driver of the Ford Ecosport car bearing No.AP-03-CB-3679 came from the opposite direction, in high speed, in rash and negligent manner.
Due to which, both the vehicles collided with each other and resulted in an accident.
Due to said impact, the deceased got fatal crushed injuries and died on the way to hospital.
10. In order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 has got examined himself as P.W.1 by filing examination-in-chief affidavit, wherein he has reiterated the entire averments made in the petition.
Further, in support of their oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked total 11 documents as Ex.P.1 to 11.

Out of the said documents, Ex.P.1 is true copy of F.I.R., Ex.P.2 and 2(a) are true copy of first information statement and its translated copy, Ex.P.3 is true copy of post-mortem report,
Ex.P.4 and 4(a) are true copy of inquest and its translated copy, Ex.P.5 is true copy of Motor Vehicle Accident report, Ex.P.6 and 6(a) are true copy of sketch and its translated copy,

Ex.P.7 is true copy of charge-sheet, Ex.P.8 and 8(a) to (c) are notarised copies of Aadhar card of petitioners No.1 to 4 and deceased, Ex.P.9 is notarised copy of death certificate of deceased T. Prakash, Ex.P.10 is notarised copy of Ration card and Ex.P.11 is notarised copy of household card.

11. At the outset it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
issuance of insurance policy in respect of Ford Eco Sport car bearing No.AP-03-CB-3679 and its validity as on the date of accident, is not in dispute.

Further, the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners has remained undisputed by the respondent No.2, who is the owner of Ford Eco Sport car bearing No.AP-03-CB-3679, as he did not choose to appear and contest the case of the petitioners.

Whereas, the respondent No.1 insurance company though has denied the involvement of its insured Ford Eco Sport car bearing No.AP-03-CB-3679 in the alleged accident and taken specific defence that, the accident has occurred due to sole rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the deceased and the driver of Ford Eco Sport car bearing No.AP-03-CB- 3679 was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and the said car was not having valid permit and fitness certificate as on the date of accident, has failed to establish the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.1, who is the representative/Deputy Manager of respondent No.1 insurance company, there is no other oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.1 to establish the said contentions or to rebut the oral and documentary evidence adduced by the petitioners.
Though the learned counsel for respondent No.1 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been elicited from his mouth which creates Bhaskar.

4 doubt on the veracity of his evidence or which goes to show that, the Ford Eco Sport car bearing No.AP-03-CB-3679 of the respondent No.2 has been falsely implicated by the petitioners in the accident in question.

12. On meticulously going through the police documents marked as Ex.P.1 to 7, prima-facia it reveals that, the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle bearing No.AP-03-BJ-9190 by the deceased T. Prakash on the wrong side of the road and dashing the same to the oncoming Ford Ecosport car bearing No.AP-03-CB-3679 of the respondent No.2.
Further it reveals that, due to the impact, the deceased T. Prakash sustained grievous injuries on his head and succumbed to said injuries on the way to hospital.

The investigation officer in his final report/charge-sheet, which is marked as Ex.P.7, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased himself and there is no fault on the part of the driver of car bearing No.AP-03- CB-3679.
13.

It is pertinent to note that, the petitioners in the present case are seeking compensation under Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, for the death of deceased T. Prakash, caused in the accident taken place on 03-08-2022 at about 2.30 p.m., in between the car bearing No.AP-03-CB- 3679 of the respondent No.2 and the motorcycle ridden by the deceased.

It is settled proposition of law that,
under Sec.164 of Motor vehicles Act, the petitioners need not require to establish that, the death is caused due to any wrongful act or negligence or default on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle or of the concerned or of any other person.
But they have to prove the involvement of offending vehicle in the alleged accident, resulting in the death of the deceased person.

14. The oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that,
the accident in question has taken place due to rash and negligent riding of motorcycle bearing No.AP-03-BJ-9190 by the deceased T. Prakash on the wrong side of the road and dashing the same to the oncoming Ford Ecosport car bearing No.AP-03- CB-3679 of the respondent No.2.
Further it reveals that, due to the impact, the deceased T. Prakash sustained grievous injuries on his head and succumbed to said injuries on the way to hospital.

The investigation officer in his Ex.P.7 final report/charge-sheet, has clearly stated that, the said accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the deceased himself and dashing the same to car bearing No.AP-03-CB-3679 of the respondent No.2.
The entire police records available on record are clear evident of involvement of insured car bearing No.AP-03-CB-3679 in the accident in question.
Admittedly, the Ex.P.7 final report/charge-sheet has neither been challenged by the petitioners, nor by the owner or driver of car bearing No.AP-03-CB-3679.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of car bearing No.AP-03-CB-3679 in the said accident, the injuries sustained by the deceased in the said accident and the cause of his death.
15.
The liability under Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, is on the principle of no fault.

The petitioners need not require to establish that, the death is caused due to any wrongful act or negligence or default on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle or of the concerned or of any other person.

The Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, reads as follows:

5 164. Payment of compensation in case of death or grievous hurt, etc. - (1)
Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act or in any other law for the time being in force or instrument having the force of law, the owner of the motor vehicle or the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay in the case of death or grievous hurt due to any accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, a compensation, of a sum of five lakh rupees in case of death or of two and a half lakh rupees in case of grievous hurt to the legal heirs or the victim, as the case may be.

sentences.text: ( 2) In any claim for compensation under sub-section (1), the claimant shall not be required to plead or establish that the death or grievous hurt in respect of which the claim has been made was due to any wrongful act or neglect or default of the owner of the vehicle or of the vehicle concerned or of any other person.

(3) Where, in respect of death or grievous hurt due to an accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle, compensation has been paid under any other law for the time being in force, such amount of compensation shall be reduced from the amount of compensation payable under this section.

16. Therefore, in the light of above provision of law and for the above stated reasons, this Court is of the considered opinion that, the petitioners have successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that, the deceased T. Prakash has succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident occurred on 03-08-2022 at about 2.30 p.m., on Madanapalle-Tirupathi NH-71 road, near coffee house, Punugupalli village, Vayalpad Mandal, Annamaya District, Andra Pradesh,
in between the motorcycle of the deceased and Ford Ecosport Car bearing Reg. No. AP-03-CB-3679 of the respondent No.2.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:

While answering above issue, for the reasons stated therein, this Court has already held that, the petitioners have successfully proved through cogent and corroborative evidence that,
the deceased T. Prakash has succumbed to the injuries sustained in an accident taken place on 03-08-2022 at about 2.30 p.m., on Madanapalle- Tirupathi NH-71 road, near coffee house,
Punugupalli village, Vayalpad Mandal, Annamaya District, Andra Pradesh, in between the motorcycle of the deceased and Ford Ecosport Car bearing Reg. No. AP-03-CB-3679 of the respondent No.2.
Now the petitioners are required to establish that, they are the legal representatives of the deceased T. Prakash.
In this regard, they have produced the notarised copy of Aadhar cards of petitioners No.1 to 4 and the deceased, notarised copy of ration card and household card of their family.

The said documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioners No.1 is father,
petitioner No.2 is mother and petitioner No.3 is sister of deceased T. Prakash.
The validity of said documents in not disputed by the respondents.
Further it is pertinent to note that, the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased is not at all denied by the respondent No.1 in the entire cross- examination of P.W.1.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the above documents produced by the petitioners and hold that, the petitioners are the legal representatives of deceased T. Prakash.
18. Further, the evidence available on record clearly establishes that, before accident the petitioners were depending on the income of the deceased.

No doubt, the P.W.1 has clearly admitted in the Bhaskar.T vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176874435/
6 cross-examination that, the petitioner No.2 is a teacher by occupation.

sentences.text: But, the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356, has clearly held that, " The legal representatives of the deceased could move application for compensation by virtue of clause (c) of Section 166(1).

entities.text: National Insurance Co. V/s Birender, reported in (2020) 11 SCC 356
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The major married son who is also earning and not fully dependant on the deceased, would be still covered by the expression "legal representative" of the deceased.
This Court in Manjuri Bera (supra) had expounded that liability to pay compensation under the Act does not cease because of absence of dependency of the concerned legal representative.
Notably, the expression "legal representative" has not been defined in the Act.
The Tribunal has a duty to make an award, determine the amount of compensation which is just and proper and specify the person or persons to whom such compensation would be paid.
The latter part relates to the entitlement of compensation by a person who claims for the same.

According to Section 2(11) CPC, "legal representative" means a person who in law represents the Tractor and Trally bearing No.AP-03-AN-8690 & AP-03-AN-8712 estate of a deceased person, and includes any person who intermeddles with the estate of the deceased and where a party sues or is sued in a representative character the person on whom the estate devolves on the death of the party so suing or sued.
Almost in similar terms is the definition of legal representative under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 i.e. under Section 2(1)(g).

As observed by this Court in Custodian of Branches of BANCO National Ultramarino vs. Nalini Bai Naique [1989 Supp (2) SCC 275, the definition contained in Section 2(11) CPC is inclusive in character and its scope is wide, it is not confined to legal heirs only.

entities.text: Custodian of Branches of BANCO National Ultramarino vs. Nalini Bai Naique [1989 Supp (2) SCC 275
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Instead it stipulates that, a person who may or may not be legal heir competent to inherit the property of the deceased can represent the estate of the deceased person.
It includes heirs as well as persons who represent the estate even without title either as executors or administrators in possession of the estate of the deceased.
All such persons would be covered by the expression "legal representative".

As observed in Gujarat SRTC vs. Ramanbhai Prabhatbhai [(1987) 3 SCC 234 a legal representative is one who suffers on account of death of a person due to a motor vehicle accident and need not necessarily be a wife, husband, parent and child.

entities.text: Gujarat SRTC vs. Ramanbhai Prabhatbhai [(1987) 3 SCC 234
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Manjuri Bera (supra), in paragraph 15 of the said decision, while adverting to the provisions of Section 140 of the Act, the Court observed that even if there is no loss of dependency, the claimant, if he was a legal representative, will be entitled to compensation.
In the concurring judgment of Justice S. H. Kapadia, as His Lordship then was, it is observed that there is distinction between "right to apply for compensation" and "entitlement to compensation".
The compensation constitutes part of the estate of the deceased.
As a result, the legal representative of the deceased would inherit the estate.
Indeed, in that case, the Court was dealing with the case of a married daughter of the deceased and the efficacy of Section 140 of the Act.
Nevertheless, the principle underlying the exposition in this decision would clearly (claimants) even though they are major sons of the deceased and also earning.
It is thus settled by now that the legal representatives of the deceased have a right to apply for compensation.

Having said that, it must necessarily follow that even the major married and earning Bhaskar.T vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176874435/
7 sons of the deceased being legal representatives have a right to apply for compensation and it would be the bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the application irrespective of the fact whether the concerned legal representative was fully dependent on the deceased and not to limit the claim towards conventional heads only."

19. According to the ratio laid down in above cited decision, the legal representatives though were not fully dependent on the income of deceased, are entitled to claim compensation under all the heads i.e., under both conventional and non-conventional heads.

Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.

Further, if the age particulars of the petitioners mentioned in the cause title of the petition is taken into consideration, it clearly goes to show that, the petitioners have lost the love and affection, as well as the care of the deceased, who was the main bread earner of the family.
By taking into consideration of all these factors along with the evidence of PW1, it is crystal clear that,
the petitioners were the dependents of the deceased during his lifetime.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled to claim compensation under the head of loss of dependency as per law.

20. As per the provision of Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, the owner of the vehicle or the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- in the case of death or and Rs.2,50,000/- in case of grievous injury, due to any accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle.
As per the said provision, there is fixed compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- to be paid in case death.

Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for just and reasonable compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-, for the death of T. Prakash in a motor vehicle accident taken place in between the motorcycle of the deceased and car bearing Reg. No. AP-03-CB-3679 of the respondent No.1.
21.

In so far as awarding of interest on the compensation is concerned in, MFA No. 103557/16 between Sri Ram General Ins. Co. Ltd., V/s. Smt. Lakshmi and Others (D.D. 20.3.2018), the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka on detailed discussions has fixed the rate of interest @ 6% p.a., holding that as per Sec.34 of C.P.C., the rate of interest that can be awarded on judgments cannot be more than 6% p.a.

entities.text: Sri Ram General Ins. Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since, Section 149 of Motor Vehicles Act provides for interest on judgments, the interest to be awarded in claim petitions has to be 6% p.a. and not more than that.
Hence, in the present case, interest @ 6% per annum on the compensation amount, is awarded.
22. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident, the respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the Ford Ecosport Car bearing Reg. No. AP-03-CB- 3679.

Further,
the evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the deceased T. Prakash has succumbed to injuries sustained in an accident taken place in between the motorcycle of the deceased and the car bearing Reg. No. AP-03-CB-3679 of the respondent No.2.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of vehicle involved in the accident is liable to compensate for the damage caused due to usage of said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the said vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

However, the Bhaskar.T vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176874435/
8 primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

entities.text: Bhaskar.T vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- from the respondent No.1, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:

In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- (Rupees five lakh only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioners.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

The above compensation amount is apportioned as follows:
Petitioner No.1 - Father - 40% Petitioner No.2 - Mother - 40% Petitioner No.3 - Sister - 20% The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest awarded in favour of petitioners No.1 to 3, shall be released to them, through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is pertinent to note that, the petitioners in the present case are seeking compensation under Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, for the death of deceased T. Prakash, caused in the accident taken place on 03-08-2022 at about 2.30 p.m., in between the car bearing No.AP-03-CB- 3679 of the respondent No.2 and the motorcycle ridden by the deceased.
It is settled proposition of law that,
under Sec.164 of Motor vehicles Act, the petitioners need not require to establish that, the death is caused due to any wrongful act or negligence or default on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle or of the concerned or of any other person.
But they have to prove the involvement of offending vehicle in the alleged accident, resulting in the death of the deceased person.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of car bearing No.AP-03-CB-3679 in the said accident, the injuries sustained by the deceased in the said accident and the cause of his death.
15.
The liability under Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, is on the principle of no fault.
The petitioners need not require to establish that, the death is caused due to any wrongful act or negligence or default on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle or of the concerned or of any other person.
As observed by this Court in Custodian of Branches of BANCO National Ultramarino vs. Nalini Bai Naique [1989 Supp (2) SCC 275, the definition contained in Section 2(11) CPC is inclusive in character and its scope is wide, it is not confined to legal heirs only.
Instead it stipulates that, a person who may or may not be legal heir competent to inherit the property of the deceased can represent the estate of the deceased person.
It includes heirs as well as persons who represent the estate even without title either as executors or administrators in possession of the estate of the deceased.
Now coming to the point of quantum of compensation for which the petitioners are entitled is concerned, every legal representative who suffers on account vehicle accident, should have remedy for realization of compensation.
Further, if the age particulars of the petitioners mentioned in the cause title of the petition is taken into consideration, it clearly goes to show that, the petitioners have lost the love and affection, as well as the care of the deceased, who was the main bread earner of the family.
By taking into consideration of all these factors along with the evidence of PW1, it is crystal clear that,
the petitioners were the dependents of the deceased during his lifetime.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled to claim compensation under the head of loss of dependency as per law.
opennyai_summary.decision:
20. As per the provision of Sec.164 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989, the owner of the vehicle or the authorised insurer shall be liable to pay compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- in the case of death or and Rs.2,50,000/- in case of grievous injury, due to any accident arising out of the use of motor vehicle.
As per the said provision, there is fixed compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- to be paid in case death.
Therefore, this Court is of the opinion that, the petitioners are entitled for just and reasonable compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-, for the death of T. Prakash in a motor vehicle accident taken place in between the motorcycle of the deceased and car bearing Reg. No. AP-03-CB-3679 of the respondent No.1.
21.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.2 being the owner of vehicle involved in the accident is liable to compensate for the damage caused due to usage of said vehicle.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer of the said vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
However, the Bhaskar.T vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176874435/
8 primary liability is on the respondent No.1 to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Therefore, for the above stated reasons, holding that, the petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- from the respondent No.1, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
23. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- (Rupees five lakh only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioners.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.1 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
The above compensation amount is apportioned as follows:
Petitioner No.1 - Father - 40% Petitioner No.2 - Mother - 40% Petitioner No.3 - Sister - 20% The entire compensation amount with proportionate interest awarded in favour of petitioners No.1 to 3, shall be released to them, through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
